Rashi on Pesachim 66a:10:1.hebrew: אלא אמר קרא - במוספין: ״עולת שבת בשבתו על עולת התמיד״ — לבד מעולת התמיד. אלמא תמיד נמי דחי:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:10:1.english: Rather, the verse states - regarding the additional [Shabbat] offerings: "The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat, beside the continual burnt-offering" — [meaning] apart from the continual burnt-offering. Thus, the continual [offering] also overrides [Shabbat].

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:11:1.hebrew: אמר מר ועוד קל וחומר כו' ופרכוה - מהא פירכא, שכן כליל, שכן תדיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:11:1.english: The Master said: And furthermore, an a fortiori inference, etc., and they refuted it - With this refutation: that [it is] wholly burnt, [and] that [it is] frequent.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:12:1.hebrew: וכי מאחר דגמיר - מרבותיו שגזירה שוה זו לכך באה — דקיימא לן אין אדם דן גזירה שוה מעצמו אלא אם כן נתקבלה ובאה מסיני, דדילמא קרא למילתא אחריתי אתא — וכיון דהוא כך קיבל, הרי הוא כמו שנכתב בגופו בפירוש, ולמה ליה קל וחומר, שהוא דבר סברא מדעתו ומלבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:12:1.english: And since he learned - from his teachers that this gezerah shavah [verbal analogy] comes for this [purpose] — as we hold [that] a person may not expound a gezerah shavah on his own unless it was received and came from Sinai, lest the verse come for another matter — and since he received it thus, it is as though it were written explicitly in its [very] text; so why did he need a kal vachomer [a fortiori inference], which is a matter of reasoning from his own mind and heart?

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:12:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר נהי דגזירה שוה לא גמריתו - מרבותיכם. גזירה שוה צריכא רב, דאין אדם דן גזירה שוה מעצמו אלא אם כן למדה מרבו; אלא קל וחומר כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:12:2.english: This is what he is saying: Granted that you did not learn the verbal analogy - from your teachers. A verbal analogy requires a teacher, for a person may not expound a verbal analogy on his own unless he learned it from his teacher; but an a fortiori [inference], etc.:

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:12:3.hebrew: אמרו לו קל וחומר - דאית ביה לא דיינינן, דפריכא הוא, כדאמרן: שכן תדיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:12:3.english: They said to him: An a fortiori [inference] - that is in [this case] we do not derive, for it is refutable, as we said: "since it is frequent."

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:1:1.hebrew: אמר לו רבי עקיבא או חילוף - או אני אחליף הדין, דפשיטא לי דהזאה מעכבא, וילפינן בקל וחומר מינה לשחיטה שתעכב:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:1:1.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: Or [the] reverse - Or I will reverse the argument, for it is obvious to me that sprinkling is prevented [from overriding Shabbat], and we derive via an a fortiori argument (kal vachomer) from it regarding slaughter, that it should [also] be prevented [from overriding Shabbat].

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:1:2.english: In its appointed time - [As it is written:] "And let the children of Israel offer the Paschal lamb in its appointed time."

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:2:1.hebrew: הבא לי מועד לאלו - שיהא זמן קבוע להן כמה שקבוע לשחיטה. הילכך, כיון דלא קביע להו זימנא, ומצי למיעבד להו מאתמול, לא דחו. והזאה נמי לאו מגופיה דפסח היא, ולא כתיב בה מועד:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:2:1.english: Bring me an appointed time for these - That there should be a fixed time for them just as [a time] is fixed for slaughter. Therefore, since no time is fixed for them, and one can perform them on the previous day, they do not override [Shabbat]. And sprinkling [purification water] as well is not part of the Paschal offering itself, and "appointed time" is not written regarding it.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:3:1.english: This law - That the Paschal offering overrides Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:3:2.english: The sons of Beteira - They were leaders [Nesi'im].

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:3:4.hebrew: וכי פסח אחד יש לנו שדוחה את השבת והלא יותר ממאתים פסחים יש לנו שדוחין את השבת - כלומר, יותר ממאתים קרבנו' יש שדוחין שבת בשנה: חמשים שבתות השנה, בכל שבת ושבת ארבעה כבשים — שנים לתמידים ושנים למוספין — הרי מאתים, לבד שבת שבתוך פסח ובתוך החג, שקריבין בהן מוספי היום: שבעת טלאים בפסח וארבעה עשר לחג:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:3:4.english: Have we [but] one Paschal lamb that overrides Shabbat? Do we not have more than two hundred Paschal lambs that override Shabbat? - That is to say, there are more than two hundred offerings that override Shabbat during the year: [there are] fifty Shabbats in the year, [and] on each and every Shabbat [there are] four lambs — two for the daily burnt-offerings and two for the additional offerings — behold, [that is] two hundred, apart from a Shabbat that [falls] during Passover and during the Festival [of Sukkot], on which the additional offerings of the day are offered: seven lambs on Passover and fourteen on the Festival [of Sukkot].

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:4:1.english: Just as “its appointed time” stated with regard to the daily offering - And later [the Gemara] asks: from where do they [derive] the daily offering itself?

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:6:1.english: And he was sitting and expounding - In the manner that the Nasi does.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:6:2.hebrew: מקנטרן - לשון קניטה ועצבון, קונטנדי"ר (קונטרריי"ר: להעליב) בלע"ז:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:6:2.english: Rebuking them - An expression of provocation and distress, contendre (contrarier: to insult) in Old French.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:7:1.hebrew: מהו - הבאת סכין אינה דוחה, דהא אפשר למיעבד מאתמול, ומה יעשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:7:1.english: What is [the law] - Bringing a knife does not override [Shabbat], since it was possible to do [it] yesterday, and what should he do?

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:7:2.english: I heard and forgot - Further on, [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:7:3.english: They are the sons of prophets - and you will see what they will do.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:1.english: The next day - On the fourteenth [of Nisan], on Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:2.english: [One] whose Paschal offering was a lamb stuck [it] in its wool - the knife.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:3.hebrew: ומי שפסחו גדי - שאין לו צמר אלא שיער, שאין יכול לתוחבו בצמרו, תחב לו בין קרניו. ואין זה משאוי לעבור עליו משום שביתת בהמתו, דלאו אורחיה בכי האי מלאכה. ובענין זה הביאו סכיניהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:3.english: And one whose Paschal offering was a goat - Since it does not have wool, only hair, so that he cannot stick it in its wool, he stuck [it] between its horns. And this is not a burden on account of which one transgresses [the prohibition of] his animal resting [on Shabbat], for this is not its [usual] manner of labor. And in this manner they brought their knives.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:4.english: He saw - Hillel [saw] this deed that they did.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:5.english: And he remembered [the] halakha - Thus I heard.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:8:6.english: Thus have I received [by tradition] - That such is the halakha, as these [people] have done.

Rashi on Pesachim 66a:9:1.hebrew: פסח נמי כתיב ביה במועדו - ולא שמעת לי' מיניה, ומתמיד ילפת ליה. אלא על כרחיך, מדבעית למילף מתמיד, לא משתמע להו דחיית שבת, דאמרי במועדו דקאמר, בזמן התירא קאמר. הכא בתמיד נמי לא משמע להו, ומנא ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 66a:9:1.english: With regard to the Paschal lamb too, “in its appointed time” is written - Yet you did not derive [that it overrides Shabbat] from it, and [instead] you derive it from the daily offering. Rather, perforce, since you needed to derive [it] from the daily offering, [the verse] does not imply to them the overriding of Shabbat, for they say [that when] it states “in its appointed time,” it means at a time that is permitted [for slaughter]. Here, with regard to the daily offering too, it does not imply [this] to them, so from where [is it derived] for it?

Tosafot on Pesachim 66a:11:1.hebrew: מה לתמיד שכן תדיר - ותימה: ונילף מבינייהו דתמיד ומילה, או משתי הלחם (גרידא), דדחו שבת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66a:11:1.english: What [is unique] about the daily offering, that it is frequent - And this is puzzling: let us derive [it] from the common feature of the daily offering and circumcision, or from the Two Loaves (alone), which override Shabbat!

Tosafot on Pesachim 66a:13:1.hebrew: תוחב לו בצמרו - וא"ת: והא בעי כלי שרת, כדילפינן בפ' דם חטאת (זבחים דף צז:) "ויקח את המאכלת"? ויש לומר שהקדישום. השתא משמע בשמעתין דיש איסור רשות הרבים בירושלים, וקשה: דאמרינן בפ' קמא דעירובין (דף ו:): "ירושלים אלמלא דלתותיה ננעלות בלילה חייבין עלי' משום רשות הרבים" — ולאו דוקא ננעלות, אלא ראויות לנעול, כדמסיק התם. ותירץ ר"י: דהכא לאחר שנפרצו בה פרצות; וכי האי גוונא משני בפרק בתרא דעירובין (דף קא) אמילתא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 66a:13:1.english: Sticks it in its wool - And if you ask: Does [slaughtering] not require a sacred service vessel, as we derive in the chapter [entitled] Dam Chatat (Zevachim 97b) [from the verse], "And he took the knife"? One can say that they consecrated them. Now, it is implied in our passage that there is a prohibition of [carrying in] a public domain in Jerusalem, and this is difficult: for we say in the first chapter of Eruvin (6b), "Jerusalem, were its doors not locked at night, one would be liable on its account for [carrying in] a public domain" — and not specifically locked, rather fit to be locked, as [the Gemara] concludes there. And the Ri answered that here [it refers to] after breaches were made in it; and similarly, [the Gemara] answers in the last chapter of Eruvin (101) regarding another matter:

Tosafot on Pesachim 66a:4:1.hebrew: מה מועדו האמור בתמיד דוחה את השבת - ולקמן יליף מעל עולת התמיד. תימא, דבשמעתין לא דריש ממשמעות דמועדו, וכן הא דפסח דחי טומאה, ילפינן לקמן מאיש איש: איש נדחה ואין ציבור נדחין, ובתמיד ילפינן מג"ש דמועדו מועדו. ובפרק כיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים דף עז.) משמע דדריש לה ממשמעות דמועדו, דתניא: "וידבר משה את מועדי ה'" — מה ת"ל? לפי שלא מצינו בכל התורה שנאמר בהן מועדו אלא בפסח ותמיד; מועדו — אפי' בשבת, מועדו — אפילו בטומאה, שאר קרבנות מנין? משמע דממשמעות' דמועדו דריש. ועוד, דקאמר התם: וצריכי, דאי כתב רחמנא תמיד — שכן תדיר וכליל, אבל פסח לא; ואי כתיב פסח — שכן כרת. ואי מגזירה שוה ילפינן, מה צריך לצריכותא? הא איצטריך מועדו דתמיד משום טומאה, ודפסח משום שבת! אלא ודאי ממשמעותא דמועדו דריש, וע"כ תנאי היא. ועוד, בפ' ר' ישמעאל במנחות (דף עב.) דריש שתי הלחם דדחו שבת מתקריב — "תקריב" אפילו בשבת ואפילו בטומאה; ולפי שמעתין מצי למילף בג"ש דמועדו מפסח ותמיד, או ממשמעותא כמו בכיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים דף עז.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 66a:4:1.english: "Just as 'its appointed time' stated with regard to the daily offering overrides Shabbat" - And later on [the Gemara] derives [that the daily offering overrides Shabbat] from [the verse] "besides the continual burnt-offering." It is astonishing, for in our sugya [the Gemara] does not expound [this] from the plain implication of "its appointed time"; and similarly, that the Paschal offering overrides impurity, we derive later on from [the phrase] "any man" [ish ish]: an individual is deferred [to Pesach Sheni], whereas a community is not deferred, and regarding the daily offering, we derive [that it overrides impurity] from a gezeirah shavah of "its appointed time" / "its appointed time." Yet in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (later in Pesachim 77a) it implies that [the Gemara] derives it from the plain implication of "its appointed time," as it is taught in a baraita: "And Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord" — what does the verse come to teach? Because we do not find anywhere in the entire Torah that "its appointed time" is stated except with regard to the Paschal offering and the daily offering: "its appointed time" — even on Shabbat; "its appointed time" — even in a state of impurity; from where [do we know this for] other offerings? This implies that [the Tanna] expounds it from the plain implication of "its appointed time." And furthermore, [this is evident] because it says there: And [both verses] are necessary, for if the Merciful One had written [only] the daily offering, [one might say that it overrides Shabbat and impurity] because it is frequent and wholly burnt, whereas the Paschal offering is not; and if [the Merciful One] had written [only] the Paschal offering, [one might say it is] because [neglecting it incurs] karet. Now, if we derive [them] from a gezeirah shavah, why is there a need for [such] a necessity argument? Surely "its appointed time" of the daily offering is needed for impurity, and that of the Paschal offering is needed for Shabbat! Rather, it must certainly be that [the Tanna there] expounds from the plain implication of "its appointed time," and perforce it is a Tannaitic dispute. And furthermore, in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael in Menachot (72a), [the Gemara] derives that the Two Loaves override Shabbat from [the word] "you shall bring near" — "you shall bring near," even on Shabbat and even in a state of impurity; whereas according to our sugya, one could derive [it] through the gezeirah shavah of "its appointed time" from the Paschal offering and the daily offering, or from the plain implication [of "its appointed time"], as in Keitzad Tzolin (later in Pesachim 77a):
